For example, locker number 6 is toggled by students 1, 2, 3, and 6. Each toggle changes the state of the locker from open to closed or vice versa. Initially, all lockers are closed. But if a locker has an odd number of factors, it will be open. Wait, but which numbers have an odd number of factors?

I think perfect squares have an odd number of factors. Because factors usually come in pairs, but for perfect squares, one of the factors is repeated (the square root). For example, 16 has factors 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The factor 4 is the square root of 16, and it's only counted once. So, all perfect squares will have an odd number of factors, and hence be toggled an odd number of times, ending up open.
